title: The Kentucky Meat Shower
hook: In 1876, chunks of red meat reportedly fell from a clear Kentucky sky.

beats.label: THE CASE
beats.line: On a farm in Bath County, meat fell from a cloudless sky.

beats.label: CLUE 1
beats.line: Flakes of flesh, some as large as a hand, covered the yard and fields.

beats.label: CLUE 2
beats.line: Neighbours reportedly tasted the meat, and said it resembled mutton or venison.

beats.label: CLUE 3
beats.line: Scientists examined samples and identified the tissue as lung, likely from a large animal.

beats.label: THEORY
beats.line: The likely explanation: a large flock of vultures overhead had vomited while roosting.

beats.label: THE TWIST
beats.line: It remains one of the strangest, and messiest, unexplained weather events on record.

end.line: Would you have believed a meat shower?

description: In March 1876, chunks of meat reportedly fell from a clear sky over a Kentucky farm. Scientists now think a flock of vultures overhead is the likely explanation.

facts.claim: On 3 March 1876, pieces of red meat reportedly fell from a clear sky onto a farm in Bath County, Kentucky.
Witnesses described flakes ranging from bite-sized to several inches across, scattered over an area reportedly about 100 by 50 yards.
Some locals reportedly tasted the meat and said it resembled mutton or venison.
Scientists who examined preserved samples identified the tissue as lung, consistent with an animal such as a horse or deer.
The most widely accepted modern explanation is that a large flock of black vultures roosting overhead regurgitated the meat.
The event remains a well-documented but unusual case in the history of reported odd falls from the sky.
